CARGO AHOY

Privacy policy

Last updated: November 13, 2026

Dunkstone (“we”), an independent game studio in Canada, makes Cargo Ahoy and is responsible for the information this policy describes. It explains what happens to your information when you play.

What the game keeps on your device

Your progress, gold, collection, settings and privacy answers are saved on your device. We don’t ask for your name, email address or an account. Settings shows a support code: a random ID made on your device. It’s attached to the game’s analytics and crash reports (below), and you can quote it when you contact us.

Ads

Cargo Ahoy shows ads, and Unity LevelPlay chooses which partner shows each one. To show and measure ads, LevelPlay and its partners may collect:

  • your device’s advertising identifier, if you allow it (on iPhone, through Apple’s tracking alert; on Android, unless you’ve deleted it in your phone’s settings)
  • your IP address, and the rough location it implies
  • your device type, operating system and language
  • which ads you saw and tapped

These are the partners that can show ads in Cargo Ahoy. Some join the auction only once we’ve linked their account, so not all of them show ads today. Each partner handles this data under its own privacy policy:

  • Unity LevelPlay and Unity Ads
  • Google AdMob
  • Meta Audience Network
  • Liftoff
  • Mintegral
  • DT Exchange
  • InMobi

Analytics and crash reports

We use Google’s Firebase to learn how the game is played and to fix crashes:

  • Google Analytics for Firebase records gameplay events, such as runs started and finished, heights reached, ads watched and purchases made, along with your support code, Firebase’s app instance ID, your device type, operating system and the rough location your IP address implies.
  • Firebase Crashlytics sends a report when the game crashes: the device, the operating system, the state of the app and your support code. It never includes your saved game.
  • Firebase Remote Config downloads the game’s settings, such as ad timing, so we can adjust them without an update.

Nothing is sent before you’ve answered the consent questions. If you refuse on our consent screen, analytics runs in Google’s consent mode, which sends events without identifiers. If you accept but don’t allow tracking in Apple’s alert, analytics still measures the game, but none of it is used for advertising. Google handles this data under the Firebase privacy and security terms and Google’s privacy policy.

Your choices

  • Consent: if your App Store country is in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, or we can’t tell where it is, the game’s own consent screen asks before any ad loads, with two equal buttons, Accept and Refuse. It appears once, the first time you leave the results of your first run. If you refuse, you still see ads, just not personalised ones, and every reward works the same. Your answer is saved on your device and passed to Unity LevelPlay, which passes it to every partner in its auction.
  • Tracking on iPhone: Apple’s alert asks whether apps may track you. Where our consent screen shows, Apple’s alert follows only if you accept, and never after you refuse. Your answer to Apple always wins: if you don’t allow tracking, accepting our consent screen doesn’t change that. You can change it in iOS Settings at any time.
  • Advertising ID on Android: you can reset or delete it in your phone’s Settings › Privacy › Ads. Ads then stop being personalised by it.
  • Changing your mind: in Europe, the UK and Switzerland, the game’s Settings shows Privacy choices, which reopens our consent screen. Settings also shows your answer to Apple’s tracking alert, which only iOS Settings can change.
  • United States: the game’s Settings shows Your Privacy Choices. There you can opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information with our ad partners. Your choice is saved on your device and passed to Unity LevelPlay at once.
  • Removing ads: Remove Ads stops interstitial ads. Ads you choose to watch stay available.

Purchases

Apple or Google handles any purchase. We never see your payment details. Unity IAP handles the store for us. To complete and restore purchases it records your purchase history and an ID for your device, under Unity’s privacy policy.

Leaderboards, reminders, ratings and sharing

If you’re signed in to Game Center on iPhone, or Google Play Games on Android, your best heights are posted to its leaderboards, under Apple’s or Google’s privacy policy. Reminders are local notifications planned on your device; the game asks before sending any (Android 13 and later ask for permission too), and we don’t run a notification server. The rating prompt and the share sheet are your phone’s own, from Apple or Google; we receive nothing from them.

Children

Cargo Ahoy is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their information. If you believe a child has given us information, contact us.

Why we may use it

  • Personalised ads and tracking: your consent, given on our consent screen and in Apple’s tracking alert. You can take it back at any time in the game’s Settings or in iOS Settings.
  • Analytics: your consent. If you refuse, Google’s consent mode measures the game without identifiers, under our legitimate interest in seeing how the game is played.
  • Ads that aren’t personalised: our legitimate interest in keeping the game free.
  • Crash reports: our legitimate interest in fixing the game.
  • Purchases and leaderboards: what’s needed to give you what you bought or chose to use.

Where we rely on our legitimate interest, you can object by contacting us.

Your rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct or delete your personal information, to object to its use, and to complain to your privacy regulator. To use these rights, contact us with the support code from the game’s Settings: it’s what links your analytics and crash reports to you, and we can delete them with it (how to ask). We don’t hold your name or email address, so requests about ad data may go to the partners above.

Transfers and retention

Google, Unity and the ad partners may process data outside your country, including in the United States. They keep it for the periods their policies state, and Google deletes our analytics data on the retention schedule set for the game. Crashlytics keeps crash reports for 90 days. We can delete your analytics and crash reports sooner if you ask. Saved game data stays on your device until you delete the game.

Contact

Dunkstone’s privacy officer answers questions and requests about your information: contact@dunkstone.com.

Changes

We’ll post any change here and update the date above.
